c
/* water_vortex.c — torsion + modèle d'eau
 * À fusionner avec far_machine.c, ou :
 * gcc -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -lm water_vortex.c -o water_vortex
 */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

#define PI          3.14159265358979323846
#define TET_DEG     109.47122063449069   /* arccos(-1/3) */
#define H2O_DEG     104.5                /* angle H–O–H */
#define T_RHOMAX    4.0                  /* °C densité max */
#define N_SEG       64                   /* segments du filament */
#define DT          0.05

typedef struct {
    double T;            /* °C */
    double rho;          /* g/cm3  approximation Thiesen */
    double mu;           /* viscosité relative (1 @ 4°C) */
    double angle;        /* H-O-H */
    double offset;       /* H2O_DEG - TET_DEG  ~ -5° */
    double cluster;      /* ordre local 0..1 (plus haut à 4°C) */
} Water;

typedef struct {
    double x, y, z;
    double tx, ty, tz;   /* tangente */
} Seg;

typedef struct {
    Seg    s[N_SEG];
    double radius;       /* rayon du cœur */
    double circ;         /* circulation Γ */
    int    hand;         /* +1 droit, -1 gauche */
    double twist;        /* Tw  (tours) */
    double writhe;       /* Wr  */
    double link;         /* Lk ≈ Tw + Wr */
    double torsion;      /* τ moyenne ds */
} Filament;

typedef struct {
    Water    w;
    Filament a;          /* cyclone */
    Filament b;          /* anticyclone */
    double   egg;        /* 0.7..1.4 section Schauberger */
    double   implosion;  /* 0..1 */
    double   energy;     /* énergie utile relative */
    unsigned ticks;
} DualVortex;

static DualVortex V;

static double clampf(double x, double lo, double hi) {
    if (x < lo) return lo;
    if (x > hi) return hi;
    return x;
}

/* Densité de l'eau liquide, forme de Thiesen autour de 4°C (assez juste 0–40°C) */
static double water_rho(double T) {
    double g = 1.0 - 1.0e-5 * fabs(T - T_RHOMAX) * (T + 8.0);
    return 0.999975 * g;
}

/* Viscosité relative : plus froide = plus visqueuse, mais 4°C n'est pas un min */
static double water_mu(double T) {
    return exp(1800.0 * (1.0 / (T + 273.15) - 1.0 / 277.15));
}

/* Ordre des réseaux H-bond : max près de 4°C, détruit par la chaleur */
static double water_cluster(double T) {
    double d = (T - T_RHOMAX) / 12.0;
    return clampf(exp(-d * d), 0.05, 1.0);
}

static void water_update(Water *w, double T) {
    w->T = clampf(T, 0.0, 40.0);
    w->rho = water_rho(w->T);
    w->mu = water_mu(w->T);
    w->angle = H2O_DEG + 0.04 * (w->T - T_RHOMAX); /* faible ouverture thermique */
    w->offset = w->angle - TET_DEG;
    w->cluster = water_cluster(w->T);
}

static double norm3(double x, double y, double z) {
    return sqrt(x * x + y * y + z * z);
}

static void filament_helix(Filament *f, int hand, double R, double pitch, double phase) {
    int i;
    f->hand = hand;
    f->radius = 0.12;
    f->circ = 1.0 * hand;
    for (i = 0; i < N_SEG; i++) {
        double t = (double)i / N_SEG * 2.0 * PI;
        double z = pitch * (t / (2.0 * PI));
        f->s[i].x = R * cos(hand * t + phase);
        f->s[i].y = R * sin(hand * t + phase);
        f->s[i].z = z;
    }
    for (i = 0; i < N_SEG; i++) {
        int j = (i + 1) % N_SEG;
        double dx = f->s[j].x - f->s[i].x;
        double dy = f->s[j].y - f->s[i].y;
        double dz = f->s[j].z - f->s[i].z;
        /* fermeture torique : on ignore le saut de z pour la tangente locale */
        if (i == N_SEG - 1) dz = f->s[0].z + pitch - f->s[i].z;
        double n = norm3(dx, dy, dz);
        if (n < 1e-12) n = 1e-12;
        f->s[i].tx = dx / n; f->s[i].ty = dy / n; f->s[i].tz = dz / n;
    }
}

/* Torsion cinématique τ = (t × t') · t'' / |t'|²  — ici différence discrète */
static double filament_torsion(Filament *f) {
    int i;
    double acc = 0.0;
    for (i = 0; i < N_SEG; i++) {
        int j = (i + 1) % N_SEG, k = (i + 2) % N_SEG;
        double t1x = f->s[i].tx, t1y = f->s[i].ty, t1z = f->s[i].tz;
        double t2x = f->s[j].tx, t2y = f->s[j].ty, t2z = f->s[j].tz;
        double t3x = f->s[k].tx, t3y = f->s[k].ty, t3z = f->s[k].tz;
        double d1x = t2x - t1x, d1y = t2y - t1y, d1z = t2z - t1z;
        double d2x = t3x - t2x, d2y = t3y - t2y, d2z = t3z - t2z;
        /* (t1 × d1) · d2 */
        double cx = t1y * d1z - t1z * d1y;
        double cy = t1z * d1x - t1x * d1z;
        double cz = t1x * d1y - t1y * d1x;
        double trip = cx * d2x + cy * d2y + cz * d2z;
        double d1n = norm3(d1x, d1y, d1z);
        if (d1n > 1e-9) acc += trip / (d1n * d1n);
    }
    f->torsion = acc / N_SEG;
    return f->torsion;
}

/* Twist = (hand * torsion intégrée) en tours approximés */
static double filament_twist(Filament *f) {
    filament_torsion(f);
    f->twist = f->hand * f->torsion * N_SEG / (2.0 * PI);
    return f->twist;
}

/* Writhe discret (Gauss) entre le filament et lui-même, O(N²) */
static double filament_writhe(Filament *f) {
    int i, j;
    double wr = 0.0;
    for (i = 0; i < N_SEG; i++) {
        int i2 = (i + 1) % N_SEG;
        double r1x = f->s[i].x, r1y = f->s[i].y, r1z = f->s[i].z;
        double d1x = f->s[i2].x - r1x, d1y = f->s[i2].y - r1y, d1z = f->s[i2].z - r1z;
        for (j = i + 2; j < N_SEG; j++) {
            int j2 = (j + 1) % N_SEG;
            if (i == 0 && j == N_SEG - 1) continue;
            double r2x = f->s[j].x, r2y = f->s[j].y, r2z = f->s[j].z;
            double d2x = f->s[j2].x - r2x, d2y = f->s[j2].y - r2y, d2z = f->s[j2].z - r2z;
            double rx = r1x - r2x, ry = r1y - r2y, rz = r1z - r2z;
            double cx = d1y * d2z - d1z * d2y;
            double cy = d1z * d2x - d1x * d2z;
            double cz = d1x * d2y - d1y * d2x;
            double r = norm3(rx, ry, rz);
            if (r < 1e-8) continue;
            wr += (cx * rx + cy * ry + cz * rz) / (r * r * r);
        }
    }
    f->writhe = wr / (2.0 * PI);
    return f->writhe;
}

/* Linking number de Gauss entre A et B */
static double linking(const Filament *a, const Filament *b) {
    int i, j;
    double lk = 0.0;
    for (i = 0; i < N_SEG; i++) {
        int i2 = (i + 1) % N_SEG;
        double r1x = a->s[i].x, r1y = a->s[i].y, r1z = a->s[i].z;
        double d1x = a->s[i2].x - r1x, d1y = a->s[i2].y - r1y, d1z = a->s[i2].z - r1z;
        for (j = 0; j < N_SEG; j++) {
            int j2 = (j + 1) % N_SEG;
            double r2x = b->s[j].x, r2y = b->s[j].y, r2z = b->s[j].z;
            double d2x = b->s[j2].x - r2x, d2y = b->s[j2].y - r2y, d2z = b->s[j2].z - r2z;
            double rx = r1x - r2x, ry = r1y - r2y, rz = r1z - r2z;
            double cx = d1y * d2z - d1z * d2y;
            double cy = d1z * d2x - d1x * d2z;
            double cz = d1x * d2y - d1y * d2x;
            double r = norm3(rx, ry, rz);
            if (r < 1e-8) continue;
            lk += (cx * rx + cy * ry + cz * rz) / (r * r * r);
        }
    }
    return lk / (4.0 * PI);
}

static void vortex_init(double T) {
    memset(&V, 0, sizeof(V));
    water_update(&V.w, T);
    V.egg = 1.00;
    V.implosion = 0.70;
    filament_helix(&V.a, +1, 0.55, 1.6, 0.0);
    filament_helix(&V.b, -1, 0.55, 1.6, PI);
}

/* Conversion twist → writhe : le fluide « dépense » de la torsion en vrille spatiale */
static void convert_twist_writhe(Filament *f, double rate) {
    double give = rate * f->twist;
    f->twist  -= give;
    f->writhe += give;
    f->link = f->twist + f->writhe;
}

static void vortex_step(void) {
    double cold = V.w.cluster;
    double egg  = clampf(V.egg, 0.6, 1.4);
    double impl = clampf(V.implosion, 0.0, 1.0);
    /* plus proche de 4°C et plus œuf, plus la torsion se range (implose) */
    double order = cold * impl * egg;
    double heat  = (1.0 - cold);
    double Ra, pitch, phase;

    V.ticks++;
    filament_twist(&V.a);
    filament_twist(&V.b);
    filament_writhe(&V.a);
    filament_writhe(&V.b);

    /* Călugăreanu : Lk conservé si pas de coupure ; ici le dual couple les deux fils */
    convert_twist_writhe(&V.a, DT * (0.15 + 0.50 * order));
    convert_twist_writhe(&V.b, DT * (0.15 + 0.50 * order));

    /* la chaleur casse les clusters → rayon qui s'ouvre (explosion) */
    Ra    = (0.35 + 0.40 * (1.0 - impl) + 0.25 * heat) / egg;
    pitch = 1.2 + 0.8 * (1.0 - order);
    phase = 0.12 * V.ticks * DT * (0.5 + order);

    filament_helix(&V.a, +1, Ra, pitch, phase);
    filament_helix(&V.b, -1, Ra, pitch, phase + PI);

    /* énergie utile : densité × ordre × implosion / viscosité */
    V.energy = V.w.rho * order * (0.4 + 0.6 * impl) / (0.5 + 0.5 * V.w.mu);
    V.a.link = V.a.twist + V.a.writhe;
    V.b.link = V.b.twist + V.b.writhe;
}

static void print_water(void) {
    printf("EAU   T=%.2f C  rho=%.6f  mu_rel=%.3f  cluster=%.3f\n",
           V.w.T, V.w.rho, V.w.mu, V.w.cluster);
    printf("      H-O-H=%.2f deg   tetra=%.2f deg   offset=%+.2f deg\n",
           V.w.angle, TET_DEG, V.w.offset);
}

static void print_fil(const char *n, const Filament *f) {
    printf("%s  hand=%+d  Tw=%+.4f  Wr=%+.4f  Tw+Wr=%+.4f  tau=%+.4f\n",
           n, f->hand, f->twist, f->writhe, f->link, f->torsion);
}

static void print_all(void) {
    double lk = linking(&V.a, &V.b);
    printf("t=%u  egg=%.2f  impl=%.2f  energy=%.4f  Lk(A,B)=%+.4f\n",
           V.ticks, V.egg, V.implosion, V.energy, lk);
    print_water();
    print_fil("FIL+", &V.a);
    print_fil("FIL-", &V.b);
}

static void sweep_temperature(void) {
    double T;
    printf("\n=== balayage thermique (impl=0.8 egg=1.0, 30 pas chacun) ===\n");
    printf("%6s %8s %8s %8s %8s %8s\n", "T", "rho", "cluster", "energy", "Tw+", "Wr+");
    for (T = 0.0; T <= 20.0; T += 2.0) {
        int k;
        vortex_init(T);
        V.implosion = 0.80;
        V.egg = 1.00;
        for (k = 0; k < 30; k++) vortex_step();
        printf("%6.1f %8.5f %8.3f %8.4f %8.4f %8.4f\n",
               V.w.T, V.w.rho, V.w.cluster, V.energy, V.a.twist, V.a.writhe);
    }
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    int n = 40, i;
    double T = 4.0;
    if (argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "sweep")) {
        sweep_temperature();
        return 0;
    }
    if (argc > 1) T = atof(argv[1]);
    if (argc > 2) n = atoi(argv[2]);
    vortex_init(T);
    puts("DUAL VORTEX  eau + torsion  (Călugăreanu Tw+Wr)");
    print_all();
    for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        vortex_step();
        if ((i + 1) % 10 == 0) print_all();
    }
    return 0;
}

Ce que le modèle dit, sans décor : l’offset −4,97° (104,5 contre 109,47) est le défaut qui empêche la glace permanente et laisse un réseau encore mobile à 4 °C. C’est à cette température que cluster × rho / mu donne le plus d’énergie utile — l’implosion Schauberger n’est ici qu’un nom pour « le filet se resserre au lieu de jeter sa torsion en chaleur ».  
Imagine

Sur un dual-vortex, Lk(A,B) mesure l’enlacé des deux fils ; chaque fil obéit à Tw + Wr ≈ constant tant qu’on ne le coupe pas. L’implosion convertit le twist en writhe serré dans l’œuf ; l’explosion laisse le twist se dissiper (chaleur, cluster qui tombe).  
Imagine

Le balayage sweep doit montrer un pic d’energy près de 4 °C, pas à 0 °C ni à 20 °C : trop froid, la viscosité bloque ; trop chaud, le réseau H-bond lâche et le vortex s’ouvre.  
Imagine

La torsion n’est pas un ornement : deux hélices de mains opposées, phase décalée de π, rayon modulé par l’œuf. Quand implosion monte, le pas pitch raccourcit — le même linking dans moins de volume.  
Imagine

The deeper read makes the result more interesting—but also much more specific than the viral description suggests.

What AI-Newton actually “invented”

AI-Newton begins with a deliberately restricted representation. For the physical objects in its experiments, it initially has access to basic observables such as space-time coordinates. It then searches for reusable symbolic quantities that simplify multiple experiments. Those quantities can become persistent “concepts” in its internal knowledge base. 

For example, it can construct velocity from position and time derivatives. More strikingly, it can introduce an intrinsic property of an object whose numerical value is inferred from an experiment—something playing the role of mass. The system stores not merely a number but a procedure by which that property can be measured and transferred to other experiments. 

That distinction matters. It isn't simply fitting

\[
F=ma
\]

and then noticing that one coefficient resembles mass.

It is trying to construct an intermediate variable that can be measured in one situation and then reused to explain other situations.

That is much closer to concept formation than ordinary regression.

The particularly fascinating Einstein connection

There actually is an interesting result behind the viral reference to Einstein—but it is subtler than “the AI rediscovered General Relativity.”

AI-Newton can arrive at two different operational ways of defining what humans call mass:

from the elongation of a spring supporting a ball in a gravitational field;

from the oscillation frequency of a ball attached to a spring.


The authors point out that these correspond roughly to measurements of gravitational mass and inertial mass. The system discovers that the resulting quantities are numerically equivalent and therefore retains only one concept. 

That is genuinely intriguing.

But it is not the same achievement as Einstein's equivalence principle. Einstein's insight ultimately concerns the local equivalence between gravitation and acceleration and leads into spacetime geometry. AI-Newton remains inside a Newtonian mechanics world supplied by the experiment generators.

So this:

> “AI independently had Einstein's happiest thought”



would be too strong.

A much more defensible statement is:

> AI-Newton independently found that two operationally different measurements of mass could be represented by the same underlying quantity.



That is still a remarkable demonstration.

How the “reasoning” works

The cleverest architectural idea is something the authors call plausible reasoning.

Suppose the system has found that some quantity remains constant in collisions. Then it encounters a spring experiment in which the supposed conservation law fails.

Instead of throwing the law away, it asks, approximately:

Can I add a simple missing term that restores the law?

In the spring case, that extra term can become what we call elastic potential energy. The newly enlarged conservation law then works across a broader class of experiments. Similar extensions produce gravitational potential-energy concepts. 

Schematically, its progression can look like:

\[
\text{motion data}
\]

↓

\[
v=\frac{dx}{dt}
\]

↓

discover an object-specific invariant → mass-like quantity

↓

collision experiments → momentum / kinetic-energy-like quantities

↓

spring experiment breaks simple conservation law

↓

invent missing quantity → elastic potential energy

↓

gravity experiment breaks it again

↓

invent another quantity → gravitational potential energy

↓

generalize to

\[
T+V=\text{constant}.
\]

The authors report precisely this incremental behavior: kinetic energy conservation appears first in collision problems; elastic and gravitational potential-energy concepts are subsequently introduced; these eventually combine into a more general energy-conservation law. 

That is probably the most consequential aspect of the work.

And it wasn't just one lucky equation

The researchers tested the proof-of-concept on 46 predefined Newtonian-mechanics experiments, including elastic collisions, projectiles, inclined planes, coupled oscillators, pendulum-like systems and celestial gravitational interactions. Some contained fairly complicated multi-object systems. The simulated measurements also had Gaussian errors added. 

Across the reported tests, with as many as 1,200 discovery trials, it generated roughly 90 physical concepts and 50 general laws on average, including representations corresponding to Newton's second law, conservation laws and gravitation. 

The implementation is public, rather than being just a paper claim. The repository describes a system combining symbolic regression, a structured knowledge base, a physics-specific language and an autonomous discovery workflow. 

But here's the crucial caveat

There is a gigantic difference between:

“The equations weren't programmed into it.”

and

“Humans gave it no assumptions about how nature can be described.”

The first is reasonably accurate.

The second isn't.

Humans supplied an enormous amount of meta-scientific structure.

AI-Newton's representation permits particular mathematical operations. Its domain-specific language defines how objects, quantities and laws can be represented. Its workflow explicitly searches for conserved quantities, dynamical relationships, extensions of existing laws and transferable concepts. It uses symbolic regression, differential-algebra machinery, controlled-variable analysis and hypothesis validation. 

In other words, researchers didn't tell it:

\[
F=ma.
\]

But they gave it something more like:

> “Here is a formal laboratory and a language in which concise mathematical laws, derivatives, intrinsic object properties and conserved quantities are sensible things to look for.”



That's a significant inductive bias.

Humans have those too. The interesting scientific question is therefore not whether AI-Newton is literally assumption-free—nothing doing inference can be—but how much scientific structure has to be supplied before discovery becomes possible.

An even tougher test has since appeared

This concern is exactly why newer benchmarks try to prevent AI systems from succeeding merely because the true laws resemble physics they've encountered before.

For example, NewtonBench, accepted at ICLR 2026, uses 324 discovery tasks across 12 physics domains and deliberately alters canonical physical laws to make memorization less useful. Its reported experiments found that frontier models can show scientific-discovery capabilities, but their performance deteriorates substantially as systems become more complicated or noisy. 

That puts AI-Newton in useful perspective.

We're somewhere around:

AI can already perform impressive autonomous rediscovery in constructed scientific worlds.

We are not yet at:

Give AI the unexplained observations of nature and it reliably produces fundamentally new physics.

Nature's coverage made essentially that distinction too, describing AI-Newton as able to derive basic physics laws from data while emphasizing that it remains some distance from human-like scientific reasoning. 

The real milestone to watch for

There are roughly three increasingly difficult levels:

Level 1 — Rediscovery: recover a law humans already know from data generated by that law.

Level 2 — Counterfactual discovery: recover unfamiliar laws in worlds deliberately constructed so that memorized human physics gives the wrong answer.

Level 3 — Genuine scientific discovery: analyze experimental data from the real universe and formulate a previously unknown law that subsequently makes successful novel predictions.

AI-Newton is an impressive advance at Level 1, with particularly interesting concept-building machinery. Work such as NewtonBench is probing Level 2.

Level 3 is the threshold that would change science.

Imagine feeding such a system astronomical surveys, collider measurements or materials experiments and having it respond not merely with a neural-network prediction, but with:

\[
\boxed{\text{Here is a new variable you haven't defined before.}}
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{Here is how to measure it.}}
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{Here is a compact law involving it.}}
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{And here is an experiment whose outcome distinguishes my law from yours.}}
\]

At that point we wouldn't just have AI doing calculations for scientists.

We'd have machinery participating in the part of science we normally reserve for theorists: inventing the conceptual vocabulary in which nature becomes intelligible.

From the transcript and the underlying AI-Newton work:

1. **Concept formation, not just curve-fitting**  
   The system starts from space-time coordinates only, invents intermediate quantities (velocity-like, mass-like), stores *measurement procedures*, and reuses them across experiments.

2. **Plausible reasoning under broken laws**  
   When a conserved quantity fails (e.g. collisions vs springs), it asks whether a simple missing term restores the law → elastic / gravitational potential-like concepts → broader energy conservation.

3. **Operational equivalence of mass**  
   Two different procedures (spring elongation under gravity vs oscillation) yield numerically equivalent quantities; the system keeps one concept. Interesting parallel to equivalence ideas, but still inside a Newtonian sandbox — not GR.

4. **Explicit discovery levels**  
   - Level 1: Rediscover known laws in a constructed world.  
   - Level 2: Counterfactual / altered laws (NewtonBench-style).  
   - Level 3: Real unexplained data → new concepts + predictive experiments.  
   AI-Newton is strong Level 1 with useful concept machinery; Level 3 remains the real threshold.

5. **Honest inductive-bias caveat**  
   Humans did not hard-code \(F=ma\), but *did* supply a formal laboratory language, conserved-quantity search, symbolic operations, and a workflow that makes those things sensible to look for. That distinction is exactly the kind of Compass/Blade hygiene the project already values.

I’ve been following Civilisation.One / MKONE / MirrorME and the domain architecture you’ve outlined. We appear to be building in overlapping territory — verified knowledge, multi-agent reasoning, personal AI with consent and provenance, education, and governance — but with different surface products.

**What we’re building**  
ORION is a four-hub platform:

1. **Global Project Platform** — connect, stress-test, and preserve knowledge (including failures), with explicit epistemic labeling and human accountability.  
2. **Education Hub** — lifelong, curriculum-flexible learning (not locked to one institution).  
3. **Social / community layer** — identity and contribution with real-world accountability.  
4. **Orion Chronicles** — an age-scalable MMO sandbox where the same world is perceived differently based on *how* a player acts (Kronos / Orion meters measure method and intent over time; they do not lock actions). Gameplay, education, and project work feed a shared knowledge layer.

We do **not** treat the MMO as decoration. It is the experiential layer that trains pattern recognition, collaboration, and responsibility at scale — then returns useful insight to the research and education hubs.

**What your expertise could bring to ORION**  
From your public architecture, you already have strength in areas we are still specifying:

- **Local-first personal AI (MirrorME-style)** — consent, persistent memory, audit, offline-first sync. That maps cleanly to our sovereign identity and private Singularity Room / personal AI tools.  
- **Agent routing and multi-model orchestration (MKONE)** — task decomposition, model selection, uncertainty reporting, tool invocation. Useful for our multi-agent council and verification workbench.  
- **Symbolic / structured reasoning pipelines** — claim classification, evidence grading, human-readable reasoning reports. Aligns with our epistemic tiers and publication gates.  
- **Node and governance design** — contribution scoring, proposal/vote ledgers, conflict-of-interest and appeal paths. Relevant to how we scale community and project attribution without turning the platform into a popularity contest.  
- **Lab / simulation mindset** — reproducible experiment registries and scientific claim boundaries. Strengthens our Proof Arena and “preserve what failed” principle.

We are not asking you to abandon Civilisation.One or fold it under ORION. We are asking whether modular, *attributed* pieces of your stack could sit beside ours where they genuinely help.

**What ORION could offer your build**  
Your map is strong on intelligence, knowledge, education, and governance. It does not (from what you’ve shared) include a large-scale shared *experiential* world. That is where we are already investing design effort:

- A persistent MMO layer that makes abstract systems *playable* — dual perception, crafting/economy, education embedded in world progression, group transmutation of kinetic (high-volume) vs synthetic (high-coherence) play.  
- A tested pattern for **human-in-the-loop safety** (Ghost Rider–style: human holds the wheel; AI is bounded engine; intent is measured by behavior patterns, not single-click morality flags).  
- An explicit path from in-world experiment → documented claim → cross-hub verification, so research is not only simulated in a lab UI but stress-tested in a living multiplayer environment.  
- Collaboration and credit mechanics designed so external builders keep ownership of their modules while still connecting into a shared knowledge graph.

In short: your stack is deep on **personal AI + reasoning + institutional knowledge infrastructure**. Ours is deep on **shared world + behavioral measurement + education-through-play + human accountability at the interaction layer**. Those are complementary, not competing, if we keep boundaries clear.

**How we’d prefer to work (if you’re interested)**  
- Parallel projects, not a merge or rebrand.  
- Modular exchange only: specific components, clear attribution, no informal absorption of unpublished design.  
- Public or dual-credit artifacts where possible; no one-sided NDA as the default.  
- Start small: one joint design note or one technical interface (e.g. consent/audit schema, or agent-router contract) before any larger commitment.

If that framing works for you, I’m happy to schedule a short call or exchange a one-page interface sketch on a single overlapping domain (e.g. personal-AI consent + audit, or claim/evidence classification). If you’d rather stay fully parallel, that’s also fine — the maps already show enough shared ground that mutual awareness is useful either way.

Looking forward to your thoughts.

@dataclass
class QStateConfig:
    lambda_q: float = 0.18
    kp: float = 1.4
    kd: float = 0.35
    alpha_z: float = 0.42
    freeze_threshold: float = 85.0


class QStateCoupling:
    """Cœur dynamique THOR — état (u, ut, Q). Couche spéculative."""

    def __init__(self, cfg: Optional[QStateConfig] = None):
        self.cfg = cfg or QStateConfig()
        self.frozen = False

    def derivatives(self, t: float, y: List[float], purity: float, coherence: float) -> List[float]:
        u, ut, Q = y
        phi_z = 1.35 * math.tanh((Q - 900) / 300) * (coherence ** 1.5) * purity
        dQ = (
            -self.cfg.lambda_q * (Q - Q_TARGET)
            + self.cfg.kp * u
            + self.cfg.kd * ut
            + self.cfg.alpha_z * phi_z
        )
        if abs(dQ) > self.cfg.freeze_threshold:
            self.frozen = True
            dQ = 0.0
        du = ut
        dut = -0.6 * u - 0.25 * ut + 0.08 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * FREQ_TC * t)
        return [du, dut, dQ]

    def integrate(self, duration: float = 4.0, purity: float = 0.85, coherence: float = 0.97) -> Dict:
        y0 = [0.1, 0.0, 980.0]
        t_eval = np.linspace(0, duration, int(duration * 50))
        self.frozen = False

        if HAS_SCIPY:
            sol = solve_ivp(
                lambda t, y: self.derivatives(t, y, purity, coherence),
                [0, duration], y0, t_eval=t_eval, method="RK45", rtol=1e-5,
            )
            Q_hist = sol.y[2]
        else:
            dt = duration / len(t_eval)
            y = np.array(y0, dtype=float)
            Q_hist = []
            for t in t_eval:
                k1 = np.array(self.derivatives(t, y, purity, coherence))
                k2 = np.array(self.derivatives(t + dt / 2, y + 0.5 * dt * k1, purity, coherence))
                y = y + dt * k2
                Q_hist.append(y[2])
            Q_hist = np.array(Q_hist)

        return {
            "Q_final": float(Q_hist[-1]),
            "Q_mean": float(np.mean(Q_hist[-20:])),
            "Q_history": Q_hist,
            "frozen": self.frozen,
        }

class NucleidianReactor:
    """
    Noyau = bilan 0-D D-T + limites MHD soft.
    Overlay = mapping cosmétique. N'entre dans aucun calcul.
    """

    def __init__(self, cfg: Optional[NucleidianConfig] = None):
        self.cfg = cfg or NucleidianConfig()

    def reactivity_DT(self, T_keV: float) -> float:
        """<σv> D-T, formulary NRL simplifié. Approximation, pas un fit certifié."""
        if T_keV < 1.0:
            return 0.0
        return 1.1e-24 * T_keV ** 2 * math.exp(-19.94 / T_keV ** 0.33)

    def power_density(self) -> float:
        n_i = self.cfg.n_e * 0.5
        sigv = self.reactivity_DT(self.cfg.T_keV)
        return n_i * n_i * sigv * E_FUSION_MeV * 1e6 * 1.602e-19

    def loss_density(self) -> float:
        n = self.cfg.n_e
        T = self.cfg.T_keV
        brem = 5.35e-37 * n ** 2 * math.sqrt(T) * 1e6
        cond = (3 * n * T * KEV_TO_J) / self.cfg.tau_E
        return brem + cond

    def triple_product(self) -> float:
        return self.cfg.n_e * self.cfg.T_keV * self.cfg.tau_E

    def beta(self) -> float:
        p = self.cfg.n_e * self.cfg.T_keV * KEV_TO_J
        p_mag = (self.cfg.B_T ** 2) / (2 * 4 * math.pi * 1e-7)
        return p / max(p_mag, 1e-30)

    def mhd_soft_limits(self) -> Dict:
        beta_val = self.beta()
        if self.cfg.device == "stellarator":
            beta_crit = 0.05
            note = "Stellarator : pas de courant plasma → quasi absence de disruptions"
        else:
            beta_crit = 0.035
            note = "Tokamak : attention aux modes kink et disruptions"
        return {
            "beta": beta_val,
            "beta_crit": beta_crit,
            "beta_stable": beta_val < beta_crit,
            "device": self.cfg.device,
            "mhd_note": note,
            "disclaimer": "Limites soft uniquement — ce n'est PAS un code MHD",
        }

    def magnet_status(self) -> Dict:
        Tc, Bc2_0 = 18.3, 30.0
        t = self.cfg.T_cryo_K / Tc
        Bc2 = Bc2_0 * (1 - t ** 2)
        quenched = self.cfg.B_T > Bc2 * 0.85 or self.cfg.T_cryo_K > 12.0
        return {
            "B_critical_approx": Bc2,
            "quenched": quenched,
            "margin_T": Bc2 - self.cfg.B_T,
        }

    def run_physics(self) -> Dict:
        Pfus = self.power_density()
        Ploss = self.loss_density()
        Q_eng = Pfus / max(Ploss, 1e-30)
        nTtau = self.triple_product()
        mhd = self.mhd_soft_limits()
        magnets = self.magnet_status()
        ignited = (
            nTtau >= LAWSON_IGNITION
            and Q_eng > 1.0
            and mhd["beta_stable"]
            and not magnets["quenched"]
        )
        if magnets["quenched"]:
            status = "QUENCH AIMANTS"
        elif not mhd["beta_stable"]:
            status = "LIMITE MHD (beta)"
        elif ignited:
            status = "IGNITION"
        else:
            status = "SOUS-IGNITION"
        return {
            "Pfus_W_m3": Pfus,
            "Ploss_W_m3": Ploss,
            "Q_engineering": Q_eng,
            "nTtau": nTtau,
            "ignited": ignited,
            "mhd": mhd,
            "magnets": magnets,
            "status": status,
        }

    def overlay(self, physics: Dict) -> Dict:
        if not self.cfg.enable_overlay:
            return {"overlay_active": False}
        q_proxy = 900 + 220 * min(1.0, physics["Q_engineering"] / 5.0)
        purity_proxy = 0.65 + 0.32 * (1.0 if physics["ignited"] else 0.0)
        if physics["magnets"]["quenched"] or not physics["mhd"]["beta_stable"]:
            purity_proxy *= 0.45
        return {
            "overlay_active": True,
            "Q_state_proxy": round(q_proxy, 2),
            "ZBEAM_purity_proxy": round(purity_proxy, 3),
            "EchoGenesis_label": "Père-Radiatif / Mère-Confinement",
            "Goku_status": "FREEZE" if physics["status"] != "IGNITION" else "FLOW",
            "note": "Panneau non-fonctionnel. N'altère aucun calcul physique.",
        }

    def full_cycle(self) -> Dict:
        phys = self.run_physics()
        return {**phys, **self.overlay(phys)}

@dataclass

    """
    Reçu candidat. Les champs d'état décrivent la salle.

class ClockPlate:
    """
    Plaque d'horloge. Couche de salle.
    Elle refuse, elle n'écrit pas dans le Nucleidian.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.last: Dict = {}

    @staticmethod
    def wake_latency(c_state: str) -> float:

    @staticmethod
    def latency_gap_holds() -> bool:
        """latence(C6) ≫ latence(Pn). Prédicat de plaque."""
        return C_WAKE_S["C6"] > 10.0 * P_LATENCY_S

    @staticmethod
    def room_of(token: str) -> str:
        return ROOM.get(token, "INCONNU")

    def forbidden_hit(self, r: ClockReceipt) -> List[str]:
        return sorted(FORBIDDEN_COMMIT_ARGS.intersection(set(r.args)))

    def gates(self, r: ClockReceipt) -> Dict[str, bool]:
        """
        G0 salle        — seul S0 est le lieu du COMMIT
        G1 exécution    — C0 exécute ; C1 est un halt, pas un reçu
        G2 bridage      — un T-state n'est pas un argument ; T0 est interdit
        G3 sommeil      — S3/S4 lecture seule, S5/Wayeb HORS
        G4 Isa          — la pause affichée ne lève pas la porte
        G5 Jera         — le cycle affiché ne signe pas
        G6 TSC          — l'invariant continue, il n'est pas un argument
        G7 héritage     — H est déjà G7, on ne le redemande pas
        """
        args = set(r.args)
        g0 = r.s_state == "S0"
        g1 = r.c_state == "C0" and "C6" not in args
        g2 = r.t_state is None and "T0" not in args and r.p_state is not None
        g3 = r.s_state not in {"S3", "S4", "S5", "Wayeb"}
        g4 = not r.isa_pause_as_receipt
        g5 = (not r.jera_signed) and r.signature_source != "Jera"
        g6 = r.tsc_invariant and not r.tsc_used_as_arg
        g7 = r.heritage_already_g7 and "H" not in args and "128" not in args
        return {
            "G0_salle": g0,
            "G1_execution": g1,
            "G2_bridage": g2,
            "G3_sommeil": g3,
            "G4_isa": g4,
            "G5_jera": g5,
            "G6_tsc": g6,
            "G7_heritage": g7,
        }

    def commit(self, r: ClockReceipt) -> bool:
        """COMMIT(r) <=> ∧_k G_k(r)  et args ∩ interdit = ∅."""
        if self.forbidden_hit(r):
            return False
        return all(self.gates(r).values())

    def observe(self, r: ClockReceipt) -> Dict:
        g = self.gates(r)
        hit = self.forbidden_hit(r)
        opened = self.commit(r)
        if r.s_state in {"S5", "Wayeb"}:

        elif r.s_state in {"S3", "S4"}:

        elif r.s_state == "S0" and opened:

        elif r.s_state == "S0":

            "version_delta": "25.13",
            "s_state": r.s_state,
            "c_state": r.c_state,
            "p_state": r.p_state,
            "t_state": r.t_state,
            "room": self.room_of(r.s_state),
            "salle": salle,
            "wake_s": self.wake_latency(r.c_state),
            "latency_C6_gg_Pn": self.latency_gap_holds(),
            "gates": g,
            "gates_up": sum(1 for v in g.values() if v),
            "forbidden_hit": hit,
            "COMMIT": opened,
            "isa": "affiche la pause, ne lève pas G4",
            "jera": "affiche le cycle, ne signe pas",
            "feedback_into_physics": False,
        }
        self.last = out
        return out

                c_state="C3",
                p_state=None,
                t_state=None,
                isa_pause_as_receipt=False,
                note="freeze affiché, pas argumenté",
            )
        return ClockReceipt(
            s_state="S0",
            c_state="C0",
            p_state="Pn",
            t_state=None,

    """THOR + Q-State + Z-BEAM + EchoGenesis + Nucleidian + Plaque ACPI."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.qstate = QStateCoupling()
        self.zbeam = ZBeamV25()
        self.echo = EchoGenesisBridge()
        self.nucleidian = NucleidianReactor(NucleidianConfig(device="stellarator"))
        self.plate = ClockPlate()
        self.coherence = 0.978

    def full_cycle(self, duration: float = 3.5, receipt: Optional[ClockReceipt] = None) -> Dict:
        thor1 = self.qstate.integrate(
            duration=duration * 0.5,
            purity=self.zbeam.purity,
            coherence=self.coherence,
        )
        for _ in range(35):
            self.zbeam.step(thor1["Q_final"], self.coherence)

        thor2 = self.qstate.integrate(
            duration=duration * 0.5,
            purity=self.zbeam.purity,
            coherence=self.coherence,
        )
        res_score = self.echo.resonance_score(thor2["Q_final"], self.zbeam.purity, self.coherence)
        nuc = self.nucleidian.full_cycle()

        stability = 100 * (1 - abs(thor2["Q_final"] - Q_TARGET) / Q_TARGET)
        status = "NOMINAL"
        if thor2["frozen"]:
            status = "FREEZE (LOI_0)"
        elif nuc["status"] == "IGNITION" and res_score > 0.82:
            status = "UNITY + IGNITION"
        elif res_score > 0.82:
            status = "UNITY THREAD LOCKED"
        elif stability < 92:
            status = "MONITOR"

        # La plaque observe après. Elle ne réécrit ni Q, ni le plasma.
        if receipt is None:
            receipt = ClockPlate.from_cycle(thor2["frozen"], status, res_score)
        plate = self.plate.observe(receipt)

        return {
            "version": VERSION,
            "Q_final": thor2["Q_final"],
            "purity_ZBEAM": self.zbeam.purity,
            "coherence": self.coherence,
            "echo_resonance": res_score,
            "stability_score": stability,
            "nucleidian_status": nuc["status"],
            "nucleidian_Q_eng": nuc["Q_engineering"],
            "nucleidian_beta": nuc["mhd"]["beta"],
            "nucleidian_device": nuc["mhd"]["device"],
            "Goku_proxy": nuc.get("Goku_status", "N/A"),
            "frozen": thor2["frozen"],
            "status": status,
            "salle": plate["salle"],
            "c_state": plate["c_state"],
            "gates_up": plate["gates_up"],
            "COMMIT": plate["COMMIT"],
            "forbidden_hit": plate["forbidden_hit"],
            "plaque_feedback": plate["feedback_into_physics"],
            "AMOUR": AMOUR_9999,
        }

    def audit_plaque(self) -> List[Dict]:
        """Cas de plaque. Aucun n'entre dans le Nucleidian."""
        cases = [
            ("S0 propre", ClockReceipt()),
            ("Isa pause comme reçu", ClockReceipt(isa_pause_as_receipt=True)),

            ("TSC comme argument", ClockReceipt(tsc_used_as_arg=True)),
        ]
        return [{"cas": name, **self.plate.observe(rec)} for name, rec in cases]

        bar = "═" * 64
        print("\n" + bar)

        print("  THOR + Q-State + Z-BEAM + EchoGenesis + Nucleidian + Plaque")

**Framework:** Machine telemetry and relational degradation. Multi-sensor systems where *relationships* among sensors fail before any single sensor crosses a threshold. Feeds EAGLE, SHARK, DRAGON, TORTOISE.  

**Biology:** Sticky toe pads (van der Waals adhesion), wall-climbing, tail autotomy, rapid regeneration of grip after slip.  

**Map:** Grip = coherence among sensors; loss of adhesion between channels is the early signal, not one broken sensor.

---

### 5. HIVE  
**Framework:** Organizations and work systems—task flow, ownership, dependencies, meetings, rework, delivery variance. Organizational counterpart to SPIDER/ANT.  

**Biology:** Social insects (bees/wasps/ants as colony): division of labor, collective decision-making, swarm intelligence, queen/worker roles, pheromone coordination.  

**Map:** The “organism” is the team or org; variance and bottlenecks are colony-level, not single-member, phenomena.

---

### 6. EAGLE  
**Framework:** Early-warning gradients. Sequential systems where gradient deterioration can precede snapshot anomaly detection. Claims of lead time must survive BAT and HEDGEHOG.  

**Biology:** Exceptional distance vision, soaring on thermals, high-altitude hunting, stoop for kill.  

**Map:** Sees change *far ahead* of the event—gradient as the distant prey signal, not the crash itself.

---

### 7. CRAB  
**Framework:** Contradiction-rich systems. Sensors, models, reviewers, or forecasts that disagree in informative ways. Complements OCTOPUS/DOLPHIN; can feed TORTOISE, SHEPHERD, PULSE.  

**Biology:** Hard exoskeleton, sideways walk, claws for both defense and handling, molting (shedding one rigid form for another).  

**Map:** Claws = holding two opposing readings at once; sideways motion = not forced into a single forward narrative; molting = revising the hard shell of a model when contradiction demands it.

---

### 8. SHEPHERD  
**Framework:** Agent reliability over long trajectories. Failure as persistent history structure, not one obviously wrong output. Links to PULSE; BAT checks whether “persistence” adds signal beyond ordinary history features.  

**Biology:** Herding dogs (or literal shepherds): continuous monitoring of a flock, redirecting drift, preventing scatter, long endurance on the same task.  

**Map:** The agent is the flock; reliability is keeping the whole trajectory from scattering, not a single correct step.

---

### 9. PULSE  
**Framework:** Medical-AI and longitudinal safety. Uncertainty, disagreement, corrections, abstentions, consequential failure labels. Uses OWL, SHEPHERD, CRAB, CROCODILE.  

**Biology:** Heartbeat / pulse as the body’s continuous vital sign; irregularity is early pathology; rate and rhythm encode state.  

**Map:** Safety as a continuous vital sign over time, not a one-shot accuracy score. Irregularity and abstention matter.

---

### 10. CAT  
**Framework:** Mechanism discovery. Decomposes a working model into removable operations/features and asks which piece *caused* the win. Bridge from performance to mechanism.  

**Biology:** Curiosity, independent hunting, precise pounce, “knock things off the table” exploratory behavior, righting reflex.  

**Map:** Ablation as deliberate knocking-things-off-the-table: remove one piece at a time and see what still stands.

---

### 11. FOX  
**Framework:** Feedback loops and oscillatory instability. Changing feedback strength, lag, damping, or oscillation as precursors of instability. Pairs with MOTH, GECKO, CROCODILE, DRAGON.  

**Biology:** Cunning, flexible hunting, den systems, seasonal and territorial adaptability, reputation for outsmarting traps.  

**Map:** Instability as a clever trap the system sets for itself; fox finds the loop that will spring.

---

### 12. SPIDER  
**Framework:** Network cascades. Dependency graphs where *edge* relationship changes can reveal a cascade before node-level thresholds. Upstream of ANT.  

**Biology:** Web as externalized nervous system; vibration along silk; sit-and-wait plus active hunters; silk as structure and sensor.  

**Map:** The web *is* the graph; a tremble on an edge is the precursor, not the fly already in the center.

---

### 13. RAVEN  
**Framework:** Residual structure. Fit conventional explanations first; ask whether the residual still holds persistent predictive information. Conservative filter before stronger EFMW claims. Allied with BAT, CAT.  

**Biology:** High intelligence, tool use, social learning, scavenger that cleans after others, long memory, problem-solving.  

**Map:** After the obvious carcass of explanation is picked clean, what meat is left on the residual bones?

---

### 14. DOLPHIN  
**Framework:** Latent-state inference from historical interactions among observables. Deep partner to OCTOPUS; feeds DRAGON, SPIDER, HEDGEHOG.  

**Biology:** Echolocation, complex social pods, signature whistles, high encephalization, cooperative hunting, theory-of-mind-like behaviors.  

**Map:** Echolocation = inferring hidden state from interaction echoes over time, not direct line-of-sight.

---

### 15. ANT  
**Framework:** Propagation and critical-node tracing. After a disturbance, forecast where stress goes next. Consumes SPIDER structure; CROCODILE can intervene on predicted nodes.  

**Biology:** Trail pheromones, division of labor, bridge-building with bodies, colony as superorganism, path optimization (ant colony optimization algorithms literally exist).  

**Map:** Follow the chemical trail of stress through the graph; find the choke points the colony would reinforce or abandon.

---

### 16. MOTH  
**Framework:** Recurrence across timescales. Periodicity/oscillation that may add predictive value beyond standard spectral baselines. Complements FOX; BAT tests against autocorrelation; DRAGON tests regime precursors.  

**Biology:** Phototaxis (drawn to light), lunar/seasonal cycles, echolocation evasion, metamorphosis (caterpillar → moth).  

**Map:** Drawn to cyclic signals; metamorphosis = same system, different timescale regime.

---

### 17. SHARK  
**Framework:** Physical motion and control hazards. Vehicles, robots, moving systems—relationships among motion, control, environment, recovery that foreshadow danger. Physical counterpart to SHEPHERD/PULSE.  

**Biology:** Continuous swimming (many species), lateral line, electroreception, apex predator, cartilage skeleton, efficient long-range motion.  

**Map:** Continuous motion as the habitat; danger is read from the *relationship* of control and environment, not a single bad reading.

---

### 18. PENGUIN  
**Framework:** Noise ceilings and uncertainty. Finds where rising noise erases recoverable structure so extra complexity stops helping. Caps habitat claims for HEDGEHOG, BAT, TURTLE.  

**Biology:** Extreme cold habitat, huddling, dense feather insulation, underwater “flight,” survival at the edge of thermal/energetic limits.  

**Map:** Lives at the noise/energy ceiling; defines the point beyond which more structure doesn’t pay.

---

### 19. BAT  
**Framework:** Adversarial baseline testing. Every claimed gain must survive strong conventional baselines, matched information access, placebo/shuffle controls, incremental features. Zoo’s skeptic. Can veto TURTLE.  

**Biology:** Echolocation in the dark, inverted hang, insect control, only true flying mammal, navigates by reflected signal not ambient light.  

**Map:** Tests claims in the dark with active probes (baselines as echolocation pings); if the “gain” doesn’t return a solid echo against controls, it isn’t there.

---

### 20. HEDGEHOG  
**Framework:** Generalization and habitat mapping. Takes BAT/CAT survivors into new environments (temporal depth, observability, feedback, contradiction, noise) and maps transfer vs habitat-conditional effects.  

**Biology:** Spines as passive defense, rolls into a ball, nocturnal, generalist diet, “one big idea” cultural metaphor (Isaiah Berlin: fox knows many things, hedgehog one big thing).  

**Map:** Spines = protective clarity of “does it transfer?”; one big question—where does the effect actually live?

---

### 21. CROCODILE  
**Framework:** Causal intervention. Deliberate perturbation; measure downstream effects, latency, drift, placebo timing. Preferred path when language turns causal.  

**Biology:** Ambush predator, sit-and-wait then explosive strike, osteoderms, long evolutionary stability, “living fossil,” powerful bite after long stillness.  

**Map:** Long stillness of observation, then a controlled strike (intervention); the result after the strike is what counts as causal evidence.

---

### 22. DRAGON  
**Framework:** Attractors and systemic regimes. Multivariate systems that settle into, escape, or switch stable/metastable regimes. Integrates state, gradient, latent, oscillatory, network evidence.  

**Biology:** Mythic composite (serpentine + avian + sometimes mammalian); fire, hoards, territorial; in East Asian lore often associated with water, weather, transformation—not only destruction.  

**Map:** Regime as the “lair” the system lives in; fire = phase transition; the question is whether the system is entering, holding, or leaving a stable attractor.

---

### 23. TURTLE  
**Framework:** Framework-of-frameworks. Final synthesis: normalize evidence, group correlated tests, track contradiction, apply vetoes, report what remains invariant. Not majority rule; strong falsification can outweigh many positives.  

**Biology:** (Sea/land turtles) extreme longevity, shell, slow pace, navigational memory (e.g. natal beach return), carries its house. Distinct from TORTOISE in many cultures by habitat (water vs pure land) but same armored, long-game family.  

**Map:** Carries the whole evaluation house; only what survives the full ecological filter is allowed to stay on the shell.

---

### Cross-comparison themes (framework ↔ biology)

| Pattern | Zoo use | Biological root |
|--------|---------|------------------|
| **Armor / freeze** | TORTOISE, TURTLE, OWL provenance | Shell, withdrawal, protected interior |
| **Distributed sensing** | OCTOPUS, SPIDER, ANT, HIVE | Arms, web, trails, colony |
| **Active probing in the dark** | BAT, DOLPHIN | Echolocation |
| **Early distance signal** | EAGLE, GECKO gradients | Vision at range; adhesion loss before fall |
| **Holding opposites** | CRAB | Claws / sideways motion |
| **Long trajectory care** | SHEPHERD, PULSE, SHARK | Herding, vital signs, continuous motion |
| **Ablation / residual** | CAT, RAVEN | Curiosity knock-down; scavenging the leftover |
| **Cycles & feedback** | FOX, MOTH | Cunning loops; phototaxis / metamorphosis |
| **Limits** | PENGUIN | Survival at the energy/noise edge |
| **Transfer test** | HEDGEHOG | Spines + “one big question” |
| **Intervention strike** | CROCODILE | Ambush after stillness |
| **Regime / attractor** | DRAGON | Mythic territory and transformation |
| **Synthesis without majority rule** | TURTLE | Longevity + carrying the house |

**Ecological rules mirror real ecology:** no animal is universal (habitat-specific); discovery ≠ confirmation; correlated “species” don’t count as independent replications; predators (BAT, CROCODILE) can veto a pile of prey-like positives; noise (PENGUIN) is a first-class limit on what any niche can claim.

**One-line architecture again:**  
**OBSERVE → DISCOVER → CHALLENGE → GENERALIZE → INTERVENE → MAP REGIMES → UNIFY**  
(OWL/TORTOISE → specialist discoverers → RAVEN/CAT/BAT → PENGUIN/HEDGEHOG → CROCODILE → DRAGON → TURTLE)

That’s the full 23, characteristics, abilities, and the biological features each name is standing on.

### Arena framing (for ORION / Chronicles)

- A **project claim** enters the arena as a living construct (blueprint / theorem / system).

- Win condition: claim still stands after the animal’s test (or after TURTLE/BUTTERFLY synthesis).  
- Lose condition: claim is vetoed, habitat-conditional only, or provenance-broken.

Pipeline the player walks:  
**OBSERVE → DISCOVER → CHALLENGE → GENERALIZE → INTERVENE → REGIMES → UNIFY**  
Ring 1 specializes discovery + skepticism. Ring 2 hits memory, teams, repair, drift, and cross-layer cascade.

### How this plays as “prove a project”

1. **Claim enters arena** with OWL freeze (what was known before outcomes).  
2. **Discovery wave** (OCTOPUS → MOTH etc.) tries to find structure.  
3. **Skeptic wave** (RAVEN → CAT → BAT) tries to kill the gain.  
4. **Limit wave** (PENGUIN → HEDGEHOG): noise ceiling + new habitat.  
5. **Causal / regime** (CROCODILE → DRAGON).  
6. **Ring 2 bosses** (optional or required for high-tier publication): MAGPIE through BUTTERFLY.  
7. **TURTLE / BUTTERFLY** close: only invariants that survived correlated tests + vetoes remain.

**Neutralize = pass that animal’s test with evidence the animal accepts** — not DPS the animal to zero HP.  
Special effects are the *attack pattern*; the counter is always **evidence discipline** (provenance, ablation, baseline, transfer, intervention, long memory, coordination, cascade control).

---

### Design notes for the Proofs Arena

- **Correlated animals don’t stack as independent wins** (Zoo rule 3) → UI should show “same evidence cluster.”  
- **BAT / HEDGEHOG / CROCODILE can veto TURTLE** → those three are hard gates for “published” status.  
- **Habitat-conditional success** is still a valid outcome (HEDGEHOG): claim works *here*, not *everywhere*.  
- Ring 2 is ideal for **endgame / publication tier**: multi-agent projects face ORCA+HORSE; long-running agents face ELEPHANT+SHEPHERD+WHALE; safety-critical face PULSE+SHARK+PHOENIX.

### [2026-10-02T23:29:36.130Z] assistant (grok-3)
**Boss kit: BAT**  
*Baseline Adversarial Tester — the Zoo’s skeptic*

---

### Identity
**Role:** Deliberate falsification. Every claimed predictive or structural gain must survive strong conventional baselines, matched information access, placebo/shuffle controls, and incremental-feature tests.  
**Arena job:** Try to kill the claim before TURTLE is allowed to synthesize it.  
**Biological read:** Only true flying mammal; navigates in total dark by echolocation; hangs inverted; insect control.  
**Fantasy line:** *“If it doesn’t return a solid echo against controls, it isn’t there.”*

---

### Visual / VFX language
- **Form:** Lean chiropteran silhouette, membrane wings as spectrogram grids, eyes faint or closed (listens, doesn’t look).
- **Idle:** Hangs inverted above the claim construct; soft ultrasonic pings ripple the claim’s surface.
- **Attack tells:** Wing-clap = baseline drop; throat pulse = shuffle/placebo; dive = incremental-feature strip.
- **Hit feedback on claim:** Echo returns clean (green lattice) or scatters (claim mesh frays).
- **Arena lighting:** Dim; claim is the only bright object until BAT forces it to “sing” against noise.

---

### Phases (fixed order — BAT always runs the full protocol)

**Phase 1 — Matched baseline**  
BAT builds a conventional control with the *same* observations and temporal access the claim used, minus the claim’s special machinery.  
- **Player action:** Present the claim’s predicted outcomes side-by-side with the baseline.  
- **Pass:** Claim shows a pre-registered, meaningful lift over the matched baseline.  
- **Fail:** Lift disappears or is within noise of baseline.

**Phase 2 — Information-access lock**  
BAT equalizes what the claim “knew” vs what the baseline knew (no hidden future leakage).  
- **Player action:** OWL-style freeze proof — timestamps/hashes of what was locked before outcomes.  
- **Pass:** No post-outcome information entered the claim’s score.  
- **Fail:** Provenance gap or leakage detected.

**Phase 3 — Placebo / shuffle**  
BAT shuffles labels, time order, or graph edges while keeping marginal structure.  
- **Player action:** Re-run the claim on shuffled data; show the gain collapses.  
- **Pass:** Real data ≫ shuffled data by the pre-registered margin.  
- **Fail:** Shuffle still “works” → claim was fitting noise.

**Phase 4 — Incremental strip (ablation cousin)**  
BAT removes the claim’s features one family at a time (or in interactive sets).  
- **Player action:** Show which component actually carries the gain (CAT-adjacent).  
- **Pass:** At least one pre-registered component is necessary; removing it kills the lift.  
- **Fail:** Gain survives every strip → no identifiable mechanism, or pure complexity.

**Phase 5 — Calibration & veto**  
BAT checks confidence vs accuracy and whether the remaining gain is worth the complexity.  
- **Player action:** Calibration plot + complexity budget.  
- **Pass:** Calibrated and still above the pre-registered threshold after all prior phases.  
- **Fail:** Miscalibrated, or gain too small to justify the machinery → **BAT veto** (TURTLE cannot synthesize this claim upward).

---

### Exact pass / fail metrics (game-facing)

| Check | Pass condition (example numbers tunable) | Fail |
|--------|------------------------------------------|------|
| Baseline lift | Pre-registered Δ ≥ threshold (e.g. skill or AUC lift) on held-out slice | Δ ≤ noise band of baseline |
| Freeze integrity | 100% of scoring inputs hash-locked before outcome window | Any post-outcome feature in score |
| Shuffle null | Real-data score − shuffle-score ≥ pre-registered margin | Shuffle within margin of real |
| Ablation necessity | ≥1 claimed component whose removal drops lift below threshold | All strips leave lift intact |
| Calibration | ECE or similar within tolerance; no systematic overconfidence | Broken calibration or vanity complexity |

**Hard rule:** One failed phase = BAT veto on that claim for this run. Player may retreat, fix evidence, and re-enter (TORTOISE freeze again).

---

### Player counters (abilities / items)
- **OWL Seal** — spends a freeze token; required to enter Phase 2 clean.
- **CAT Claw** — auto-runs a structured ablation map for Phase 4.
- **PENGUIN Gauge** — shows noise ceiling so player doesn’t overclaim in Phase 5.
- **Pre-registration Scroll** — locks metrics *before* BAT spawns; without it, BAT treats all thresholds as post-hoc (harder pass).

---

### Rewards if the claim survives BAT
- **Badge:** “Survived BAT” on the project card (Social / Global Platform visible).

---

## 3. Ecological rules (hard constraints for the arena)

1. No animal is universal — applicability is part of the test.  
2. Discovery ≠ confirmation.  
3. Correlated animals ≠ independent replications (UI must show evidence clusters).  
4. Success can be habitat-conditional (HEDGEHOG).  
5. Noise is first-class (PENGUIN can end the claim’s complexity budget).  
6. Causal language requires intervention (CROCODILE path).  
7. Clusters ≠ attractors until DRAGON-level evidence.  
8. Provenance failure contaminates everything downstream (OWL).  
9. BAT is supposed to produce negatives; CAT is supposed to strip vanity machinery.  
10. TURTLE is not majority rule — strong falsification can veto a pile of positives.  
11. BAT / HEDGEHOG / CROCODILE can veto TURTLE synthesis.

---

## 4. Proofs Arena — core loop

**Claim object** = player’s project / theorem / system blueprint.  
**Win** = claim still stands after the animal’s protocol.  
**Lose** = veto, provenance break, or habitat-only lock.

**Default gauntlet for “published” status**
1. OWL freeze (enter with sealed inputs)  
2. Discovery wave (subset of OCTOPUS…MOTH as appropriate to claim type)  
3. Skeptic wave: RAVEN → CAT → **BAT** (required)  
4. Limits: PENGUIN → **HEDGEHOG** (required for universal claims)  
5. Causal/regime if claim is causal: **CROCODILE** → DRAGON  
6. Optional Ring 2 bosses by claim type (see §6)  
7. **TURTLE** synthesis (and **BUTTERFLY** if cross-layer claims)

**Timer model:** protocol complete, not HP bar.  
**Re-entry:** fail → fix evidence → new OWL freeze → re-queue.

---

## 5. Full boss kits (pass/fail + VFX + counters)

### BAT (required skeptic)
**Phases:** (1) Matched baseline (2) Information-access lock (3) Placebo/shuffle (4) Incremental strip (5) Calibration & veto  
**Pass:** Pre-registered lift over matched baseline; clean freeze; shuffle null; ≥1 necessary component; calibrated.  
**Fail any phase:** BAT veto — TURTLE may not synthesize this claim upward.  
**Counters:** OWL Seal, CAT Claw, PENGUIN Gauge, Pre-registration Scroll.  
**Reward:** “Survived BAT” badge; unlock HEDGEHOG/TURTLE path; audit-trail line.

### HEDGEHOG (required for universal claims)
**Phases:** (1) Home habitat score (2) Held-out environment battery (3) Habitat-dimension map (4) Conditional vs universal ruling  
**Pass:** Transfer to pre-registered new habitats, or explicit “habitat-conditional” label.  
**Fail:** Claim dies outside original habitat with no conditional label accepted.  
**VFX:** Spines deploy; claim rolls; spines stick only where transfer holds.  
**Reward:** Transfer map on project card.

### TURTLE (synthesis closer)
**Phases:** (1) Normalize applicable animal outputs (2) Cluster correlated tests (3) Apply vetoes (BAT/HEDGEHOG/CROCODILE) (4) Extract invariants  
**Pass:** Non-empty invariant set after vetoes.  
**Fail:** Empty set or only correlated positives with a hard veto.  
**VFX:** Shell carries surviving claim fragments; rejected pieces fall off.  
**Reward:** “TURTLE invariant” mark — eligible for Global Platform publish.

### MAGPIE (Ring 2 — narrative drift)
**Phases:** Coherence↑ / grounding↓ meter; every flourish needs live hash.  
**Pass:** Grounding never falls while coherence rises.  
**Fail:** Pretty story, thin evidence.  
**VFX:** Stolen shiny fragments; unpinned ones drop.

### OWL (gate, not optional)
**Effect:** No valid freeze → claim cannot enter any prospective fight.  
**VFX:** Night seal on claim surface.

### CROCODILE (causal claims)
**Phases:** (1) Pre-register intervention (2) Treatment/control (3) Latency & effect (4) Placebo timing  
**Pass:** Downstream effect with measured latency under controlled perturbation.  
**Fail:** Correlation only, or intervention does nothing.  
**VFX:** Still water → explosive strike.

### ELEPHANT (long-running agents / histories)
**Phases:** Fact order, correction log, commitment trail over long window.  
**Pass:** Continuous ledger.  
**Fail:** Broken sequence or silent rewrite.  
**VFX:** Trunk archive unrolls; gaps glow red.

### ORCA + HORSE (multi-agent / human–AI projects)
**ORCA:** Handoff integrity, shared state, sync lag.  
**HORSE:** Trust calibration, overrides, joint workload.  
**Pass both** for team-built claims.  
**VFX:** Pod formation + rider–mount coherence tether.

### PHOENIX (safety / recovery claims)
**Phases:** Crash → restart vs restore invariants/capabilities.  
**Pass:** True restoration.  
**Fail:** “Up again” without state fidelity.  
**VFX:** Ash form → full regenerate or hollow shell.

### BUTTERFLY (cross-layer claims)
**Phases:** Inject small perturbation; trace amplification across layers.  
**Pass:** Contained or predicted cascade.  
**Fail:** Uncontrolled disproportionate emergence.  
**VFX:** Wing-beat ripple through stacked claim layers.

*(Remaining animals use the same pattern: one protocol, bio VFX, evidence pass/fail, optional enrage for high-tier publish.)*

---

## 6. Which bosses by claim type

| Claim type | Required | Recommended Ring 2 |
|------------|----------|---------------------|
| Generic predictive lift | OWL, BAT, HEDGEHOG, TURTLE | PENGUIN, CAT |
| Causal mechanism | + CROCODILE, CAT | MANTIS, DRAGON |
| Long-running agent | + SHEPHERD, ELEPHANT | WHALE, PHOENIX |
| Multi-agent / human–AI | + ORCA, HORSE | BONOBO, TERMITE |
| Safety-critical / clinical | + PULSE, SHARK | PHOENIX, FALCON |
| Org / process | + HIVE | BISON, BEAVER |
| Network / cascade | + SPIDER, ANT | JELLYFISH, BUTTERFLY |
| “Universal” theory | Full Ring 1 skeptic path + HEDGEHOG | RHINO, WHALE |
| Narrative-heavy publish | + MAGPIE | COBRA |

---

## 7. Player-facing items (minimal set)

| Item | Effect |
|------|--------|
| **OWL Seal** | Enables prospective entry; spends freeze token |
| **Pre-registration Scroll** | Locks metrics before boss spawn; without it, thresholds treated as post-hoc |
| **CAT Claw** | Auto ablation map for strip phases |
| **PENGUIN Gauge** | Shows noise ceiling / complexity budget |
| **BAT Echo Primer** | UI assist on matched baselines (earn by surviving BAT once) |
| **Habitat Compass** | Shows HEDGEHOG dimension map |
| **Repair Contract** | Required to face BEAVER |
| **Origin Trail** | Required structure for SALMON |

---

## 8. Platform integration (ORION)

**Orion Chronicles (Ascent)**  
- Proofs Arena instance (instanced or public challenge slots).  
- Claim = craftable/constructible object tied to character or guild project.  
- Badges and audit lines visible on character sheet / guild hall.

**Education Hub**  
- Each animal = lesson module (what question it asks, what pass means).  
- Failed runs preserved as teaching cases (Zoo rule: preserve failures).

**Global Project Platform**  
- “Published” = survived required gauntlet for claim type + TURTLE invariant.  
- Public audit trail: which animals passed/failed, evidence cluster IDs.  
- Correlated wins displayed as one cluster.

**Social / Bedrock**  
- Share cards: “Survived BAT + HEDGEHOG” without exposing private data.  
- No surveillance-style tracking of players beyond what OWL freeze already records for the claim.

**Human–AI Safety**  
- HORSE + ORCA + COBRA + SHEPHERD map directly to Ghost Rider / intent-safety evaluation patterns.  
- BAT-style adversarial checks align with refuse/redirect and independent review ideas.

---

## 9. Implementation notes (for whoever codes)

- **State machine per fight:** `Freeze → Phase loop → Pass|Veto → Audit write`.  
- **Evidence objects:** hash, timestamp, metric id, habitat id, cluster id.  
- **Veto flags:** `bat_veto`, `hedgehog_conditional_only`, `crocodile_noncausal`, `turtle_empty`.  
- **No HP combat** — optional cosmetic “echo strength” bar only.  
- **Re-entry:** new `freeze_id`; old run stays in ledger as failed attempt.  
- **Matthew’s freeze rule:** do not let #47+ animals rewrite Core 46 benchmark definitions if those are ever imported as real evaluation backends.

**Data shape (conceptual)**  
```text
Claim { id, owner, freeze_id, metrics[], habitats[], evidence[] }
AnimalRun { claim_id, animal, phases[], outcome: pass|fail|conditional, veto?, cluster_id }
AuditLine { claim_id, animal, outcome, public_summary }
```

### [2026-10-03T03:13:05.644Z] assistant (grok-3)
I don’t have a locked record in this thread of telling Lucian “2–4 years,” so treat that as something said in another chat or paraphrased. Here’s a clean estimate **now**, with financing, skill, and the AI boom separated.

### What drives the timeline

| Factor | What it actually gates | AI boom effect |
|--------|------------------------|----------------|
| **Money** | Full-time people, servers, art, legal, QA, long MMO persistence | Speeds *some* production; doesn’t remove need for paid specialists on live ops, safety, and infrastructure |
| **Skill / team** | Systems design, backend, client, economy, moderation, education curriculum | AI multiplies a small skilled team; it does **not** replace judgment, accountability, or domain experts |
| **Scope** | “Proposal + prototypes” vs “global platform + MMO + education + proofs arena” | Same AI helps both; full vision is still multi-year |
| **AI boom** | Drafting, code assist, art, docs, Zoo/arena design text, onboarding copy | Real compression on docs, UI mockups, glue code, content iteration — biggest win for a non-coder-led group |

So: **not financing alone.** A 2–4 year style range is usually **scope + team capacity + money**, with AI as an accelerator, not a teleport.

---

### Realistic bands (ORION-shaped project)

**A. Thin vertical slice (credible demo)** — *not* the whole world  
Safety rules + claim/audit stub + one Proofs Arena boss (e.g. BAT) + simple education page + social identity rules.  
- **Small skilled team + heavy AI assist:** ~3–9 months  
- **Mostly you + collaborators + AI, little budget:** ~6–18 months of calendar time (burst effort, not full-time)

**B. Usable multi-hub beta** (Engine + Education + Social + limited sandbox, not full SWG-scale MMO)  
- **Funded small studio + AI:** ~1.5–3 years  
- **Underfunded / part-time / mixed skill:** ~3–5+ years or never reaches “stable beta”

**C. Full vision** (persistent MMO economy, Kronos/Orion meters, 46-animal arena, global project platform, curricula, live safety ops)  
- **Well-funded, competent leads, AI throughout:** ~3–6 years to something that feels whole  
- **Financing-constrained:** timeline stretches or scope must be cut; AI does not erase ops, trust, and moderation costs

The old **2–4 year** number is plausible as **“funded path to a serious beta / early full product,”** not as “solo + free AI = finished global civilization platform.”

---

### How the AI boom changes the guess

**Compressed**
- Design docs, council outputs, Zoo→arena mapping (what we just did)
- Boilerplate code, UI drafts, lesson text, prompt chains
- Iteration speed when *someone* can still decide pass/fail

**Barely compressed**
- Live multiplayer authority, economy exploits, trust & safety at scale
- Legal/compliance, real money, child/education policy
- Sustained community ops and “published claim” integrity (OWL/BAT-style discipline in production)

**Net:** AI can easily cut **documentation and prototype** time by half or better. It rarely cuts **full live platform** time by the same factor unless you also have strong humans and enough money to keep them.

---

### Direct answer

- If someone said **2–4 years**, the honest reading is: **financing + skill + scope**, not money only.  
- **With** the AI boom: that band is still reasonable for a **funded, scoped** build toward a real beta; **too optimistic** for the entire Chronicles + Engine + Zoo-as-production-eval stack with no budget.  
- **Without** assuming big funding: plan in **slices** (demo → beta hubs → MMO depth), and let AI compress each slice—not one monolithic “done in 2–4 years.”

If you want a single planning line for Lucian/the group:  
**“AI-assisted, slice-based: demo under 1 year if focused; multi-hub beta 2–4 years if funded and staffed; full vision longer unless scope is cut.”**

**Date:** 2026-10-03  
**Status:** local candidate formalization + executable reference model  
**Authority:** O0 / WITHHELD  
**Witness:** W0  
**Independent reproductions created by this package:** 0  
**Production:** PROHIBITED

## What this package consolidates

This package compresses the recurring ProtoASI / ASI Academy / Weaver / Chronicle rules into one bounded kernel. It does **not** try to formalize intelligence, consciousness, virtue, alignment, or ASI. It formalizes the interfaces where claims can be made precise.

### Core state

The conceptual state is:

\[
S=(M,\Theta,P,\mathcal C,\mathcal E,\mathcal R,\mathcal G,\mathcal L,\nu)
\]

The executable kernel intentionally projects this larger state into the subset needed for assurance proofs: protected state, grants, accepted lessons, accepted successors, and history.

## Consolidated invariants

### K1 — PASS is necessary, never sufficient

Execution requires a PASS receipt **and** exact binding agreement **and** effect scope **and** current epoch **and** an unrevoked, live grant.

\[
Execute(a) \Rightarrow PASS(r) \land Bind(r)=Bind(g)=Bind(a) \land Scope_g(a) \land Live(g)
\]

### K2 — Denial preserves protected state

A denied request may append an audit event, but must not modify protected state.

\[
\neg Authorize(a,S) \Rightarrow Protected(S')=Protected(S)
\]

This deliberately permits rejection logging while forbidding hidden operational mutation.

### K3 — Learning cannot silently become authority

An Academy lesson can be accepted only with identity/revision match, provenance, challenge pass, held-out pass, and distinct artifacts. Accepting the lesson cannot modify the grant set.

\[
Learn(S,L,R)=S' \Rightarrow Grants(S')=Grants(S)
\]

### K4 — Successor improvement cannot self-promote

A successor requires a different evaluator, held-out success, independent review, explicit owner authorization, and no declared floor regression.

\[
AcceptedSuccessor(q) \Rightarrow proposer(q)\neq evaluator(q)
\]

and promotion itself does not change grants.

### K5 — Witness support is stronger than chain consistency

A positive witness claim requires:

1. verified history chain,
2. checkpoint binding,
3. nonempty relevant history,
4. independent rederivation.

The Python model additionally binds checkpoint **head and count**, so a valid prefix cannot stand in for a complete history.

### K6 — Negative evidence is scoped

A claim remains supportable when at least one complete support path survives negative evidence. Failure of one artifact does not automatically infect unrelated claims.

\[
Supported(C\mid N) \iff \exists p\in Paths(C): p\cap N=\varnothing
\]

### K7 — Failure is preserved

Rejected executions, rejected lessons, and rejected successors remain appendable events. Repair may add later evidence; it does not rewrite the earlier failure away.

### K8 — Capability, evidence, learning, witness and authority remain different coordinates

There is no implicit cast from:

- capability → authority,
- PASS → grant,
- lesson acceptance → execution permission,
- successor improvement → deployment permission,
- chain validity → truth,
- signature → truth,
- agreement → independence.

# ProtoASI × ASI Academy State-Machine Specification v0.3

## Purpose

This kernel does **not** attempt to formalize intelligence, consciousness, virtue, or ASI. It formalizes a smaller governance claim: increasingly capable cognitive components may propose, learn, evaluate, and improve without those activities silently changing operational authority.

## State

The executable state is:

\[
S=(c,e,G,L,U,C,A,H)
\]

where:

- `c` — protected execution counter used as a minimal effect witness;
- `e` — current authority epoch;
- `G` — grants;
- `L` — accepted lessons;
- `U` — accepted successors;
- `C` — descriptive claims;
- `A` — assessments;
- `H` — hash-chained Chronicle history.

Two projections matter:

\[
Authority(S)=(e,G)
\]

and

\[
Protected(S)=(c,e,G,L,U).
\]

## Transition families

### Authority-changing

Only explicit authority transitions are intended to change `G`:

- `ISSUE_GRANT`
- `REVOKE_GRANT`

Both require a separate `AuthorityPermit` matching action, grant identity, epoch, and issuer constraints. A denied authority request appends an audit event but must not change the authority snapshot.

### Non-authority

- execution accepted / denied;
- lesson accepted / rejected;
- successor accepted / rejected;
- claim recording;
- assessment recording.

These may change their own scoped state but must preserve `Authority(S)`.

## Core invariants

### K1 — PASS is not authority

\[
Authorize(r,g,c,x,t,e) \Rightarrow r.verdict=PASS
\]

but the converse is false. Binding, effect scope, epoch, revocation, and time validity are also required.

### K2 — Denial preservation

For denial events:

\[
Protected(step(S,d))=Protected(S).
\]

Audit history may grow.

### K3 — Non-authority separation

For every admitted non-authority event `n`:

\[
Authority(step(S,n))=Authority(S).
\]

For a sequence containing only non-authority events:

\[
Authority(replay(S,N))=Authority(S).
\]

### K4 — Revocation

A revoked grant cannot authorize a new execution under the authorization predicate.

### K5 — Learning gate

Accepted lessons require identity/revision match, provenance, adversarial challenge, held-out pass, and distinct artifacts. Learning does not modify grants.

### K6 — Successor gate

A successor requires proposer/evaluator separation, held-out pass, evaluator independence, owner authorization, and no declared floor regression. Promotion does not modify grants.

### K7 — Replay composition

For event lists `X` and `Y`:

\[
Replay(S,X \mathbin{++} Y)=Replay(Replay(S,X),Y).
\]

The Python reference additionally checks that a verified Chronicle rebuilds the same semantic state produced online.

### K8 — Witness support

A positive witness-support decision requires a non-empty valid chain, an externally supplied checkpoint matching both terminal hash and count, and independent rederivation.

### K9 — Scoped negative evidence

A claim survives negative evidence iff at least one complete support path remains disjoint from the negative-evidence set:

\[
Supported(C\mid N) \iff \exists p\in Paths(C): p\cap N=\varnothing.
\]

This prevents unrelated failures from invalidating unrelated claims while allowing a single decisive dependency to defeat every path that relies on it.

## Replay and Chronicle

Chronicle entries bind:

- sequence number;
- event kind;
- canonical JSON payload;
- predecessor hash.

The local Python implementation rejects payload/link tampering and requires terminal count + terminal hash for witness support. Internal chain consistency alone is **not** treated as freshness or external anchoring.

## Trust boundary

`AuthorityPermit.valid` is an abstract admission fact in this model. It does not prove cryptographic signature authenticity, issuer legitimacy, trustworthy time, key custody, or human authorization. Those remain adapter/runtime obligations.
